--- order: 1 unit: data introduces: [vue-app, vue-ref, vue-text] recipes: [vue-on] title: "Data on the page" summary: "Make a Vue app, keep data in refs, show it on the page with {{ }}, and see the page change by itself when the data changes." language: html voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-dom" 8131 url: http://127.0.0.1:8131/index.html ready: HTML and JavaScript code layout: full pacing: keyDelayMs: 6 explainPicture: page.html#run explainClip: query: {code: "", zoom: 1.4} caption: "Change the data, and Vue changes the page" clip: - caption: "The page shows the score in double curly brackets." - type: {into: "HTML and JavaScript code", text: "
\n

Score: {{ score }}

\n \n
\n", append: true} - caption: {text: "Load Vue, the file beside the page.", say: "Load view, the file beside the page."} - type: {into: "HTML and JavaScript code", text: "\n\n", append: true} - click: "Run ▶" - expect: {selector: "#status", contains: "Running"} - wait: 300 - click: {selector: "button", preview: true} - click: {selector: "button", preview: true} - click: {selector: "button", preview: true} - expect: {selector: "p", contains: "Score: 3", preview: true} - caption: "Each click changes the score; the page follows." - wait: 300 hook: "Apps like a basket, a chat or a scoreboard show data that keeps changing. Vue keeps the page in step with it for you." --- In the DOM course, changing the page took two jobs: change the variable, then put it on the page with `textContent`. Vue does the second job for you: ```html

Score: {{ score }}

``` `{{ score }}` shows the data and keeps it up to date. The data lives in the app's `setup`, made with `ref` so that Vue **watches** it: ```js const score = ref(0); return { score }; // the names the page can use ``` `@click="score++"` on the button changes the score when it is clicked. Copy it for now; lesson 3 is all about events. The console says you are running a **development build** of Vue: the version with extra warnings to help you. You can ignore that line. ## Predict ```step stage: predict code: page.html#predict insight: "Students who learned textContent expect the page to stay at 0; seeing it follow the data is the whole idea of Vue." check: type: predict q: "You click Add a point three times. What does the page show?" options: ["Score: 3", "Score: 0, because no line sets the text", "Score: {{ score }}", "Score: 111"] actual: "Score: 3. Each click changes score, and Vue changes every {{ score }} on the page to match." ``` There is no `textContent` anywhere in this code. ## Run ```step stage: run code: page.html#run try: { playground: dom, starter: "page.html#run", height: 420 } check: { type: reflect, text: "I clicked the button and saw the page follow the score." } ``` Press **Run** and click the button. Then change `"Quiz night"` to another title and run again. ## Investigate ```step stage: investigate code: page.html#run insight: "createApp looks after everything inside #app; ref makes data Vue watches; setup returns the names the page can use; {{ }} shows them and keeps them up to date." tasks: - check: type: match q: "Match each part with what it does." pairs: - ["createApp({ … }).mount(\"#app\")", "Vue looks after everything inside the #app div"] - ["const score = ref(0);", "data that Vue watches, starting at 0"] - ["return { title, score };", "the names the page can use"] - ["{{ score }}", "shows the data, and keeps it up to date"] - ["@click=\"score++\"", "changes the data when the button is clicked"] explain: "Data in setup, the page in #app. Change the data, and Vue changes the page." - check: type: question q: "In the DOM course, which line would this page also need?" options: ["scoreEl.textContent = score;", "const score = ref(0);", "createApp(…)", "None: it would need fewer lines"] answer: 0 explain: "Without Vue you change the variable, then put it on the page yourself. Vue does the second job." - check: type: bug code: page.html#bug text: "The page shows Score: 0, and clicking does nothing. There is no red error. Click the line that is wrong." answer: 11 fault: logic misconception: vue-plain-variable explain: "let score = 0 is a plain variable, so Vue does not watch it. The click changes it, but Vue never knows. Make it with ref(0)." ``` ### Which part does what? Data, names and the page. ### Without Vue What would you have to write? ### Spot the bug The score never moves. ## Modify ```step stage: modify insight: "New data is a ref returned from setup; the page can show it anywhere with {{ }}." try: { playground: dom, starter: "page.html#run", height: 420 } tasks: - hint: - "A second button can change the same data the other way." - "Copy the button and change score++ to score--." expected: page.html#sol-minus check: { type: code, text: "Add a Take a point button.", rules: { contains: ["score--"] } } - hint: - "New data needs three things: a ref in setup, its name in the return, and {{ }} on the page." - "`const team = ref(\"Owls\");` then `return { title, team, score };` then `

Team: {{ team }}

`" expected: page.html#sol-team check: { type: code, text: "Show a team name, kept in a ref called team.", rules: { contains: ["team = ref(", "{{ team }}"] } } ``` ### Take a point The other direction. ### A team name New data, start to finish. ## Make: a counter of your own ```step stage: make insight: "Goals only: two refs, shown with {{ }}, each changed by a button." try: { playground: dom, starter: "page.html#make", height: 420 } check: { type: code, text: "Show two pieces of data with {{ }}, each with a button that changes it.", rules: { contains: ["ref(", "{{", "@click"] } } ``` Lives and level, likes and dislikes, goals for two teams: make **two refs**, return them, show them with `{{ }}`, and give each a button. ## Where this leads ```step stage: info check: type: question q: "Your page needs to show a list of players, one line each. What would you rather write?" options: ["One line that says: one
  • for each player", "One
  • for each player by hand", "createElement in a loop, as in the DOM course", "A bigger {{ }}"] answer: 0 explain: "Next lesson: v-for makes a tag for each item in a list, and keeps it in step as the list changes." ``` Next: **lists and choices**, with `v-for` and `v-if`. ```teacher summary: Students make a Vue app, predict that the page follows the data with no textContent, match the parts of the app, find a plain variable Vue does not watch, add a button and new data, and make a two-value counter. time: 50 timing: Predict and Run 10 min · Investigate 15 min · Modify 10 min · Make 15 min goals: - I can make a Vue app and keep its data in refs. - I can show data on the page with {{ }}. - I can explain why the page changes by itself when the data changes. before: > Read the unit primer first. A Vue app has two halves. The **page** is ordinary HTML inside `
    `, with `{{ name }}` wherever a value should appear. The **setup** function makes the data with `ref(...)` and returns the names the page may use. `createApp({ setup() { … } }).mount("#app")` joins them. When a ref changes, Vue redraws the parts of the page that show it: students never write `textContent`. `vue.js` sits beside the page in the playground (it is served from this site). On a real site you would use Vue's file from vuejs.org or a build tool; teacher notes later in the course say more. The console shows one line about a **development build**: that is the version with friendlier warnings, chosen on purpose. `@click="score++"` is a recipe in this lesson (events are lesson 3). The planted bug is a plain `let` variable: the click changes it but Vue is not watching, so the page never updates and there is no error. That is the most important idea in the course: Vue only keeps up with data it watches. running: - "Predict: ask students who did the DOM course which line they expect to need." - "Run: change the title in setup and run again; nothing else on the page needs to change." - 'Investigate: for the bug, ask "how does Vue know the score changed?"' - "Modify: new data is three edits: the ref, the return, the {{ }}. Write them as a checklist on the board." - "Make: ask each student which button changes which ref." struggle: Students forget one of the three edits (ref, return, {{ }}) and the value does not show. Ask them to point to all three for each piece of data before you look at the code. stuck: - see: The page shows {{ score }} as text. ask: "Is the vue.js line there, and does the app mount on #app?" fix: Load vue.js before the script, and keep the {{ }} inside the div with id app. - see: A value is blank and the console warns it was accessed but is not defined. ask: Is its name in the return? fix: "Add it: return { title, score, team };" - see: Clicks do nothing and there is no error. ask: Was the data made with ref? fix: const score = ref(0); a plain let is not watched. stretch: Show the score twice on the page (in the title and a paragraph) and watch both follow. Add a button that doubles the score. support: Give the finished run page and ask students only to add the Take a point button. leads: "Next lesson: lists with v-for and choices with v-if. Class idea: list three apps and name the data each one keeps." exit: q: What two things must you do so a value in setup appears on the page and stays up to date? a: Make it with ref and return it from setup, then show it with {{ name }} inside the app. explain: > 1. The page shows the score with `{{ score }}`. 2. Load Vue, the `vue.js` file beside the page. 3. In `setup`, the score is a `ref`: data that Vue watches. Return it so the page can use it. 4. Each click changes the score, and Vue changes the page. No `textContent`. solutions: step-4#t1: page.html#sol-minus step-4#t2: page.html#sol-team step-5: page.html#sol-make sources: - title: "Vue.js: Quick Start (using Vue from a script tag)" url: https://vuejs.org/guide/quick-start.html#using-vue-from-cdn checked: 2026-10-12 - title: "Vue.js: Reactivity fundamentals (ref)" url: https://vuejs.org/guide/essentials/reactivity-fundamentals.html checked: 2026-10-12 ```
